text:
sarah: Legal just flagged an embargoed dataset from last year's acquisition — they want a temporary retention exception and an audit trail that proves we can delete once embargo lifts. Can someone confirm RBAC scope changes and KMS access needed?

miguel: ok — what's the embargo window and who needs access?

sarah: embargo until 2026-09-01, legal and compliance need read-only replay access + ability to request deletion manifests. They also require proof that we rotated keys and can perform a cryptographic delete/rotate flow.

olivia: for read-only replay we should avoid broad role grants. Suggest a scoped role: replay.viewer with no write; add timebound membership via SSO group.

raj: agree. Also need to ensure audit logs capture key unwrap operations and KMS decrypt requests. Our current KMS audit exports to cloud-logs but retention is 90d — legal wants 2 years for this case.

sarah: ugh — can we extend retention for just that KMS resource?

miguel: technically we can export to a long-term bucket with lifecycle rules. That bypasses the global setting. But we should create a dedicated bucket with ACL locked to security+legal.

sec-bot: ACTION CREATED: ticket SE-4621 created to implement timebound RBAC, KMS audit export bucket, and deletion manifest workflow. Assignee: dave-oncall. ETA: 3 business days. :robot_face:

dave-oncall: taking it. Quick notes: 1) I'll add replay.viewer SSO group and a temporary binding for legal. 2) I'll provision audit-export-bucket with encryption and disable public access. 3) For cryptographic proof of deletion we should publish signed manifests showing key-rotation events — propose a small lambda that snapshots key versions to the bucket and signs with our audit key.

olivia: for the temporary binding, use expiry in the SAML assertion provisioning or schedule a terraform apply with a TTL resource tag so it auto-removes.

raj: on the KMS rotate/delete proof — remember some clouds don't actually zero-key material; we need to rely on key state plus access revocation and signed manifests. Legal needs wording we can provide. I can draft the statement for the manifest.

sarah: thanks. Can you also confirm if embeddings or derived artifacts live in other places (search index, cache) that require explicit scrub?

miguel: good call — there are nightly redis caches and an embeddings bucket. I'll enumerate and add to the ticket checklist.

dave-oncall: ETA update: planning to push the RBAC binding + audit export today, bucket + lambda tomorrow, legal draft with manifest wording by EOD tomorrow. If anything blocks, will escalate.

sec-bot: REMINDER: please add all changes to SE-4621 and tag @legal @compliance in the ticket for review.

sarah: perfect. tagging here so legal sees progress: @legal-team please chime in on the manifest wording when ready. :eyes:

raj: draft paragraph for legal (will paste into ticket): "We confirm that keys associated with the embargoed dataset will be rotated and key material retired according to [KMS vendor] practices; a signed deletion manifest will be published to an access-restricted audit bucket containing timestamps, rotated key version IDs, and operation signatures. This manifest constitutes our proof-of-deletion for the embargoed dataset, subject to verification of associated snapshot deletions across storage and caches."

olivia: nit: include a clause about retention of audit manifests and who can request access (legal+security) to avoid indefinite public exposure.

miguel: added cache/embeddings sweep to checklist. If legal approves wording, we'll schedule the run after rotation.

sarah: thanks team — going to update legal and close loop once SE-4621 shows completed. :thumbsup:
